description:
`_load_parquet_via_chunked_csv` hardcodes `batch_size=200_000`.  The comment
says this keeps each HTTP request "well under 50 MB", but that budget assumes
a narrow schema (~250 bytes/row).

The tpcds_obt table is a very wide denormalized OBT with 50+ columns.  At
200k rows × ~250 bytes/column × 50 columns = ~2.5 GB, far exceeding the
budget.  In practice pandas' CSV representation is lighter, but the estimate
is schema-dependent and unverifiable without the actual row width.

Hardcoded batch sizes also prevent operators from tuning the chunk count vs.
memory tradeoff for their specific hardware and workload.

Flagged during Phase 1 remediation review (2026-04-16) as a nit.

anti_patterns.dont: add parquet_chunk_rows to the CLI --platform-option help text for other platforms
anti_patterns.why: this is QuestDB-specific, scoped to questdb.py only

preserves.behavior: All existing TestLoadParquetViaChunkedCsv tests continue to pass
Default behaviour unchanged: parquet_chunk_rows defaults to 200_000
